source.title: Stochastic Optimization of Tree Tensor Networks
source.authors: Marius Willner; Maximilian Karl Scharf; A. Uschmajew; Timo Felser; Marco Trenti

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test accuracy for several optimizers and concludes their convergence and generalization are comparable, but it does not test random-label memorization or the specified optimizer comparisons against SGD. This qualifies what its own optimizer results establish.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out accuracy by optimizer and dataset, but not training-versus-test error gaps, random-label fitting, or a comparison between adaptive optimizers and SGD. Optimizer-specific values are shown in figures; prose gives only aggregate descriptions. Compression accuracy is a downstream measure and is not included as a result bearing on these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam with Riemannian optimizers for TTNs, but none of its comparisons tests V1–V8. In particular, it has no SGD or momentum-SGD comparator for V4. Its introductory statements about gradient noise and generalization do not supply a test of V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the Riemannian optimizers have convergence and generalization comparable to Adam on the tested tasks, while producing TTNs with better numerical stability for downstream operations requiring orthogonalization. Adam is faster; its downstream instability is especially severe for deeper TTNs.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains tree tensor networks, including a hybrid CNN-TTN classifier, with Riemannian optimizer variants and compares them with unconstrained Adam. It does not reproduce the claim's experiments or its optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and TTN depth/size differ across experiments; the authors suggest deeper trees may amplify numerical problems for unconstrained optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam and the four Riemannian optimizer variants reach approximately 89% test accuracy on Fashion MNIST, just above 80% on CIFAR10, and just below 80% on Imagenette after 30 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested Riemannian TTN optimizers achieve final held-out accuracy comparable to unconstrained Adam on these three classification tasks.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say code will be released upon journal acceptance
record.problems: The optimizer accuracy comparisons are primarily presented in figures, while prose reports only approximate aggregate outcomes; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper does not report training error alongside test error for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Compression accuracy and tensor norm results in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Figures 6, 10, and 12 concern downstream numerical stability/compressibility, not the specified generalization-gap versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity. The motivation for adding CNN features to a TTN does not establish this comparison.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, including tuning, weight-decay, switching, and language-model conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty; batch size is fixed at 256.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures. Tensor norms and compression stability do not measure these.
Removal of memorized training examples versus random removal, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T5 classification to discusses/T6. Similar accuracy among these optimizers neither supports nor challenges V4 without its specified SGD comparison. A training–test gap is not required to test V4; the missing comparator is decisive here. Compression and norm results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and corresponding test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning, and broader-tuning, weight-decay, switching, and language-model conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout versus no dropout across training-set sizes and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
